text:
Hotel breakfast, or breakfast where Osaka's chefs shop? 🐟

Hotel breakfasts are comfortable, and on most mornings that's exactly what you want.

But on one morning of your trip, we'd gently suggest something different. Leave the buffet, take the subway a few minutes, and eat where the city's restaurant cooks buy their fish.

You can have scrambled eggs anywhere in the world. This one you can only have in Osaka.

━━━━━━━━━━
🏮 KIZU WHOLESALE MARKET
━━━━━━━━━━

A private wholesale market with more than 300 years of history.

Every morning, chefs from Osaka's restaurants come here for fish, vegetables and dried goods. Visitors can walk in and buy too.

It's quieter and less polished than the famous markets. No big signs, no crowds of tour groups. Just a working market getting on with its day, and that's exactly why we love sending people here.

━━━━━━━━━━
🚇 HOW TO GET THERE
━━━━━━━━━━

• Osaka Metro Midosuji or Yotsubashi Line to Daikokucho
• Take Exit 1
• About 3 minutes on foot

━━━━━━━━━━
⏰ WHEN TO GO
━━━━━━━━━━

• Best between 8:30 and 10:30
• Stalls open around dawn for the chefs, and many close by late morning, so don't sleep in
• Closed Sundays and national holidays, some Wednesdays, and 31 Dec – 4 Jan
• The calendar is on kizu-ichiba.com. Check it the night before so you don't arrive to closed shutters

━━━━━━━━━━
🍣 HOW WE'D SPEND THAT MORNING
━━━━━━━━━━

1️⃣ Skip the buffet just for this one day
2️⃣ Ride the subway to Daikokucho
3️⃣ Walk the aisles slowly and watch the market at work
4️⃣ Sit down to a seafood bowl
5️⃣ Head back into the city with the whole day still ahead of you, and a breakfast you'll actually remember

━━━━━━━━━━
➕ TWO MORE LOCAL MARKETS
━━━━━━━━━━

🥩 Tsuruhashi Market
A maze of covered lanes right outside Tsuruhashi Station, full of yakiniku restaurants, Korean grocers and fish stalls. Come hungry in the evening. Many small shops prefer cash.

🛍️ Tenjinbashisuji
A 2.6 km covered shopping street that locals use every day. About 40 minutes end to end, and a lovely walk when it rains.

Full guide with all three markets and the best time for each 👉 https://japanbystation.com/osaka-local-markets

Would you give up one hotel breakfast for this? 👇
